key_insight: A discrete adjoint built directly from GSIS enables efficient gradient-based gas-flow optimization across rarefied and continuum regimes while preserving the primal solver’s acceleration structure.
engineering_relevance: The method supports aerodynamic and thermal shape optimization and precise gas-flow allocation in manufacturing chambers.
method: Express kinetic and macroscopic GSIS equations as a fixed-point system.
Include both residual sets in a discrete Lagrangian to derive coupled adjoint equations.
Alternate kinetic and macroscopic adjoint updates using established discrete adjoint techniques.
evidence_signal: NACA0012 sensitivities closely match central finite differences with convergence in tens of iterations; capsule optimization reduces peak heat flux by 6.54–14.17%, while chamber optimization lowers wafer-pressure variation from 1.49% to 0.06%.
watch_item: Implementation requires consistent differentiation and coupling of both kinetic and macroscopic discrete residuals; broader performance beyond the reported cases remains unestablished.
paper_title: Discrete adjoint method for the general synthetic iterative scheme for optimization of rarefied and continuum gas flows
